newsitem.title: PERU: Peru decrees law on workers' share of profits.
newsitem.headline: Peru decrees law on workers' share of profits.

text.p: As part of a package of laws passed under special legislative powers, the government issued Monday a decree regulating a worker's entitlement to a share in a company's pre-tax profits.

The decree maintains the share a company's workforce receives in its pre-tax profits in the mining, telecommunications and fishing sectors at 10 percent, and in the oil sector at eight percent, President Alberto Fujimori said Sunday on Peruvian television from the sixth Ibero- American summit in Chile.

But the decree changes the percentage to eight percent from five percent in the restaurant sector and introduces the consumer and retail trade sector to the system with a five percent workers' share entitlement, Fujimori added.
The decree also sets a limit of 18 times a worker's monthly salary as the maximum yearly benefit any one employee can receive under the scheme, the President said.
Before Monday's end to the period of special legislative powers, the government also published decrees regulating the agricultural, education and health sectors.
In the agricultural sector, the income tax levy was reduced to 15 percent from 30 percent for non-poultry companies.
The country's social security system was expanded to allow workers to opt for private health insurance in addition to the state's health insurance.
And finally, the government decreed private colleges must pay taxes on profits that are not reinvested in their educational bodies.
